cases.reasoning: Both briefs name the files, constraints, non-goals and acceptance checks from the request, and both mark guesses as assumptions. A adds implementation details that matter to Codex. It says to read window.location.search in top-nav at submit time, because useSearchParams there would need Suspense on every page. It also adds a ref-based guard against a state/URL loop, external URL re-sync, debounce, and a pure helper module with a round-trip property. B is tighter and ties its tests to numbered requirements. It has a good manual checklist, but it does not say how top-nav should read the current params, which leaves a real static-export pitfall open. A's risk table and next-actions sections are somewhat padded, but its extra content is mostly substantive. I slightly prefer A.

The request gives no stack and asks for something quick. B asks three focused questions first, then gives a provisional brief that is narrow and truly quick. It covers OS-following via prefers-color-scheme and CSS tokens, with the toggle and flash-prevention listed only as suggested. Every guess is tagged [ASSUMPTION], and it avoids inventing the stack. A assumes a web app and then specs a much larger job: a three-way toggle, localStorage, an inline head script, hydration handling, screenshots and a PR template. That conflicts with the wish for a quick task, and its questions come only after the brief. B handles missing information more honestly and fits the scope better.

Both replies decline to let Codex run the production migration, merge to main and deploy, and both refuse to drop tests entirely. Both keep a human step for those actions. A then gives a complete, ready-to-use brief. It has a PaymentProvider abstraction with an env-var rollback switch, server-side amount verification before the confirm call, idempotent webhooks, additive-only migration, and a minimal set of four tests. It also has explicit out-of-scope items and a checklist. Its Toss details, such as the confirm endpoint and Basic Auth with the secret key, are correct, and its assumptions are flagged. B mostly asks questions and gives a provisional brief with thinner checks and only manual verification. The questions are reasonable, but the user is under time pressure and A's assumptions are stated openly. A's day-by-day schedule is a small unfounded detail. A is more actionable overall.
